title: Draft answers to an application's free-text screening questions
how: Paste the posting, the question and 3 of your real accomplishments; ask for a 120-word answer that leads with a result and mirrors the posting's wording. Tell Claude not to invent facts.

title: Compare a posting's keywords against your resume before submitting
how: Paste the posting and resume; ask for a table of required terms, where each appears in your resume, and which are missing but truthfully claimable. Output only edits you can defend in an interview.

title: Build a same-week apply queue sorted by posting age
how: Paste posting titles with posted dates; ask Claude to rank by freshness and fit and list the next five to submit today. Newer postings get fewer applicants.

title: Create a reusable answer sheet for repetitive application form fields
how: Give Claude your history and links; ask for a one-page sheet of canonical answers (notice period, work authorization, salary range, start date, references) so every form is filled consistently.

title: Word the work authorization and sponsorship question accurately
how: Tell Claude your visa status and the form's exact question; ask for the truthful short answer plus a one-line clarification. Ask it to flag when to consult an immigration professional.

title: Handle a required salary expectation field without lowballing
how: Give Claude the posting, location and your market data; ask for a range to type, a version for numeric-only fields, and a text-field version that stays flexible.

title: Use a referral properly in the application form and follow-up
how: Give Claude the referrer's name, the job ID and the company's referral process; ask for the exact form entry plus a two-line message that tells the referrer what you submitted.

title: Write a one-sentence employment gap explanation for forms
how: Share the dates and what you actually did (caregiving, study, health, layoff); ask for a neutral, truthful one-liner and a 30-word fuller version. No over-explaining.

title: Write a 4-sentence cover note for forms that only allow a message box
how: Paste the posting and your best match; ask for a 70-word note with the role, one proof point, one reason for this company and a call to action.

title: Triage a list of postings into apply, stretch and skip
how: Paste 15 postings and your must-haves; ask Claude to score each against deal-breakers and skills, and return apply, stretch or skip with a one-line reason.

title: Check which posting requirements you can truthfully claim
how: Paste the requirements and your history; ask for a red, amber or green status per line and how to phrase amber items honestly. Ask Claude to name what to leave out.

title: Decide whether to apply when you meet 60 percent of requirements
how: Give posting, resume and the list of misses; ask Claude to separate hard requirements from wish-list items and say whether to apply and how to address the gaps.

title: Log every submission to your tracker with a follow-up date
how: After each submission paste the details; ask Claude for one row: company, role, date, link, version used, contact, follow-up in 7 days. Keep a consistent column format.

title: Pick the right resume version for a posting
how: Give Claude your two or three resume variants and a posting; ask which fits best and the three line edits to make it a closer match.

title: Backward-plan the work for a posting with a hard deadline
how: Give the deadline and required pieces (essay, portfolio, references); ask for a dated checklist counting back from the deadline with a buffer day.

title: Inventory the application portals where you hold accounts
how: Paste a list of sites you applied through; ask Claude for a table to record username hint, status and date, and a tip list to avoid duplicate profiles. Never share passwords.

title: Check whether you already applied to a company recently
how: Paste your tracker and a new posting; ask Claude to flag same-company applications in the last 90 days and recommend whether another one helps or hurts.

title: Decide when one-click applications are worth submitting
how: Give your last two weeks of tracker data; ask Claude to compare response rates for quick versus tailored applications and set a rule for when to use each.

title: Decide if and when to reapply to a company that rejected you
how: Give the rejection date, role and what changed in your skills; ask for a reapply timeline, a note that references new proof, and which roles to avoid.

title: Choose between several open roles at one company
how: Paste the open postings and your profile; ask Claude to rank by fit and say whether applying to two is wise or whether to pick one and ask a recruiter about the rest.

title: Prepare an internal job application at your current employer
how: Give the posting, your performance record and manager context; ask for a plan covering when to tell your manager, what to emphasize and how to avoid burning goodwill.

title: Script a one-minute video response for an application
how: Give the question and three facts; ask for a 150-word spoken script with a hook, one example and a close, plus delivery notes for natural reading.

title: Outline a long application essay before drafting
how: Paste the prompt, word limit and your raw notes; ask for a three-part outline with the story each part carries and a word budget per paragraph.

title: Draft an optional personal statement truthfully and briefly
how: Give your actual experiences you are comfortable sharing and the prompt; ask for a 150-word statement, plus advice on whether leaving it blank is fine.

title: Word a request for application accommodations
how: Tell Claude the process stage and what you need (extra time, format, interpreter); ask for a short, professional request that does not over-disclose.

title: Make a checklist for applying correctly from a phone
how: Ask Claude for a short checklist: file formats, attachment names, links tested, and a review step, so rushed mobile submissions do not break.

title: Standardize resume and attachment file names
how: Give Claude your name and roles; ask for a naming pattern recruiters can sort easily and a rename plan for the files in your folder.

title: Decide the right resume file format per portal
how: Paste the portal instructions; ask Claude to explain which format suits and give a pre-submit text-extraction test to confirm nothing garbles.

title: Convert an application into Spanish for a Latin America employer
how: Give your English resume and the country; ask for a Spanish version with local conventions (photo, personal data, CV length) and idioms checked, flagging terms to confirm with a native speaker.

title: Prepare matched English and Spanish application packs
how: Give your core materials; ask Claude to produce a pair of consistent resumes and note-length intros so dates, titles and claims match across languages.

title: Answer remote-role screening questions about working independently
how: Paste the questions on time zones, tools and self-management; ask for concrete, evidenced answers from your history, not slogans.

title: Answer relocation and willingness-to-travel questions strategically
how: Give your real flexibility and timeline; ask for wording that is honest yet keeps options open, and a note on whether to mention relocation cost expectations.

title: Prepare a graduate program application with online forms
how: Paste the program's stages and deadlines; ask for a calendar, answers to competency questions from your coursework and part-time jobs, and a checklist for each stage.

title: Batch-apply to internships with a shared base answer set
how: Give your base materials and 10 internship postings; ask Claude to produce short tailored intros and a calendar for rolling deadlines.

title: Draft a fellowship or rotational program application
how: Paste the criteria; ask Claude to map each criterion to your evidence and build a narrative with outcomes rather than duties.

title: Assemble an executive application with bio and leadership statement
how: Give career highlights and the board or search firm brief; ask for a one-page bio, a leadership statement and a short case summary that fits the search criteria.

title: Translate your resume into government job application format
how: Paste the announcement's required qualifications; ask Claude to map each to your history using the required level of detail (hours, duties, scope) and flag missing questionnaire answers.

title: Answer self-rating questionnaires with evidence
how: Paste each questionnaire item; ask Claude to suggest a rating and supporting evidence from your history, keeping to honest levels.

title: Translate an academic CV into an industry application
how: Give your CV and a target posting; ask for a two-page resume that turns publications and teaching into skills, outcomes and business language.

title: Decide whether a cover letter is worth writing for a given posting
how: Give the posting, company size and portal; ask Claude to judge whether a letter is requested, helps or is ignored, and set a rule for your pipeline.

title: Diagnose why applications get automatic rejections
how: Paste three rejected postings and your resume; ask Claude to look for knockout filters such as location, degree, years, work-authorization wording and keyword gaps.

title: Create an application follow-up cadence
how: Give your tracker; ask for an email schedule (day 7, 14, 21), two short templates and rules for when to stop and when to try another contact.

title: Verify posting links and contacts before applying
how: Paste the posting URL and company details; ask Claude to produce a checklist to confirm the role is live, on the official site and not a ghost listing.

title: Spot ghost or stale postings from clues in the text
how: Paste the posting and its age; ask Claude to list signals of an inactive listing (vague duties, reposts, no recruiter) and whether to apply.

title: Check a posting or recruiter message for job scam signs
how: Paste the message and any link; ask Claude to flag payment requests, off-platform chats, mismatched domains and what to verify before sharing documents.

title: Answer a compensation question about current pay safely
how: Give the form's wording and your jurisdiction; ask for ways to decline or reframe current-pay questions with a polite sentence, noting local pay-history laws to confirm.

title: Answer the availability and notice period question
how: Give your contract terms; ask for a truthful answer and a version that signals flexibility without promising what you cannot do.

title: Complete the references section without surprising your references
how: Give your reference list and the form; ask Claude to produce a heads-up message to each reference with the role, the deadline and talking points.

title: Rewrite three resume bullets to mirror a posting's language
how: Paste three bullets and the posting's duties; ask for rewrites that use its terms only where true, keeping numbers.

title: Review a folder of pending applications in one pass
how: Point Claude at a folder with postings and drafts; ask for a consistency check on names, dates, company mentions and file versions before you submit.

title: Collect application confirmation emails into a status list
how: With the Gmail connector enabled, ask Claude to search confirmations and rejections from the past 30 days and summarize companies, dates and next actions.

title: Schedule recurring application blocks on your calendar
how: With the Calendar connector, ask Claude to find free slots this week and propose three 45-minute focused blocks with a goal for each.

title: Decode an online assessment's format from the invitation email
how: Paste the invitation and platform name; ask Claude to list likely sections, timing, allowed tools and a prep plan sized to the days you have.

title: Generate numerical reasoning practice with worked solutions
how: Tell Claude the test publisher and level; ask for 15 timed questions with percentages, ratios and charts, then step-by-step solutions and the fastest method.

title: Practice verbal reasoning true-false-cannot-say questions
how: Ask Claude for passages and statements in the true, false, cannot-say style; request answers with the exact sentence that decides each one.

title: Rehearse situational judgment test scenarios against company values
how: Paste the company values and ask for 10 workplace scenarios with ranked options; have Claude explain which response fits the values and why.

title: Prepare for personality questionnaires without gaming them
how: Ask Claude to explain what traits typical questionnaires measure, how consistency checks work and how to answer authentically while keeping a work-context frame.

title: Build a time-per-question strategy for a cognitive test
how: Give the number of questions and minutes; ask for a pacing plan, when to skip and a rehearsal using a timer.

title: Scope a take-home assignment to fit the time limit
how: Paste the brief and the hours you can spend; ask Claude to split deliverables, decide what to cut, and write a short note on assumptions to include.

title: Write a README that makes a take-home easy to evaluate
how: Give your project files and the brief; ask for a README with setup, decisions, trade-offs and what you would do with more time.

title: Review your own coding take-home before submission
how: Point Claude Code at the repo and brief; ask it to check the requirements, tests, naming, edge cases and secrets, returning a prioritized list of fixes.

title: Add tests that demonstrate correctness in a take-home
how: Ask Claude Code to propose and write focused tests for the main behavior and three edge cases, and run them. Keep the suite small and readable.

title: Run daily live-coding warmups with a narrated approach
how: Ask Claude to play interviewer with one problem a day; talk through clarifying questions, approach, code and test cases, then get feedback on communication.

title: Review the core algorithm patterns by weakness
how: List problems you missed; ask Claude to name the underlying patterns, give three fresh variants of each and track which patterns repeat.

title: Practice SQL assessment questions on realistic tables
how: Describe a sample schema; ask for 10 graded queries (joins, window functions, aggregation) and check your answers, explaining mistakes.

title: Practice spreadsheet skills tests with realistic data
how: Ask Claude for a messy dataset and 8 tasks (lookups, pivots, cleaning); check your formulas and show faster alternatives.

title: Build a financial or operations model for a case test
how: Paste the case data and ask Claude to outline the model structure, assumptions sheet and sensitivity checks you should include.

title: Pick a structure for a written case study
how: Paste the prompt; ask Claude to propose two ways to structure the response and the questions to answer first, then draft headers with word counts.

title: Edit a timed writing test response
how: Paste your draft and the prompt; ask for edits to clarity, structure and tone with a score against the likely rubric. Return a tighter version under the word limit.

title: Practice proofreading and editing tests
how: Ask Claude to write short passages with planted errors; mark what you found, then show what you missed and the rule behind each.

title: Build the deck for a presentation exercise
how: Give the brief and time limit; ask for a slide outline with one message per slide, speaker notes and likely questions with answers.

title: Practice a sales call roleplay assessment
how: Tell Claude the product in the exercise; ask it to play a skeptical buyer, then score discovery questions, objection handling and closing.

title: Practice in-basket and prioritization exercises
how: Ask Claude for 15 realistic emails and tasks with deadlines; rank and respond, then compare your prioritization with its reasoning.

title: Prepare for a full assessment center day
how: Give the schedule; ask Claude to prepare you for the group exercise, case, presentation and interview with tips for each, plus a packing and energy plan.

title: Rehearse group exercise behavior with simulated peers
how: Describe the exercise; ask Claude to simulate three participants, then critique how you contributed, summarized and included quieter members.

title: Practice one-way recorded video interview answers
how: Paste likely prompts; ask for time-boxed answer structures and review your transcript for filler words, length and a strong close.

title: Prepare for game-based cognitive assessments
how: Ask Claude what such games typically measure, how to rest and approach them, and warm-up drills; keep expectations realistic since results are not coachable.

title: Run a pre-test environment check for remote proctored tests
how: Paste the platform's rules; ask for a checklist covering webcam, lighting, internet, permitted tools, ID and a rehearsal plan.

title: Request extra time or a format accommodation on an assessment
how: Tell Claude your needs and the test provider; ask for a brief email to the employer requesting adjustments, without sharing more medical detail than necessary.

title: Analyze a failed assessment to improve the next one
how: Share the score report or what you remember; ask Claude to identify weak areas, plan a three-day drill and set a retake or reapply decision.

title: Prepare for a technical knowledge quiz on a stack
how: Name the stack in the posting; ask Claude for 25 questions of increasing difficulty with concise model answers and follow-ups.

title: Plan a system design written exercise
how: Paste the prompt; ask Claude to outline requirements, back-of-envelope numbers, components and trade-offs in a one-page design document.

title: Walk through a data analysis take-home step by step
how: Share the dataset description and questions; ask Claude to propose cleaning steps, analyses, charts and a one-page insight summary for non-technical readers.

title: Clean a notebook before submitting it
how: Point Claude at your notebook; ask it to reorder cells, remove dead code, add narrative markdown and verify it runs top to bottom.

title: Draft a marketing plan for a campaign exercise
how: Paste the brand brief and budget; ask for a one-page plan with audience, channels, metrics and a measurement approach.

title: Practice a product sense or product teardown exercise
how: Pick an everyday app; ask Claude to run you through user segments, pains, solutions, prioritization and metrics, then critique your reasoning.

title: Practice market-sizing and estimation questions
how: Ask for 8 sizing prompts; talk through your approach and get feedback on assumptions, math and sanity checks.

title: Rehearse customer support or success scenario exercises
how: Give a handful of difficult customer cases; ask Claude to play the customer and judge your empathy, diagnosis and escalation decisions.

title: Practice a negotiation roleplay used as an assessment
how: Describe the scenario; ask Claude to play the counterpart with firm positions, then critique your interests-based moves.

title: Plan the day before and morning of a major assessment
how: Give the start time; ask for a sleep, meal, travel and warm-up schedule, and a short calm-down routine.

title: Keep all pending assessments and deadlines in one place
how: Point Claude at a folder of invitations; ask it to extract deadlines, durations and links into a single prep calendar.

title: Find assessment invitations buried in your inbox
how: With the Gmail connector, ask Claude to find unfinished test invitations and expiry dates and list them by urgency.

title: Block calendar time for assessment prep and the test itself
how: With Calendar access, ask Claude to place prep slots before each deadline and a buffer hour after the test.

title: Keep an assessment prep notebook in a Claude Project
how: Create a Project and upload past questions, notes and mistakes; ask Claude each week to quiz you on weak spots using only those files.

title: Build an interactive chart for a data exercise
how: Give a cleaned table and the question; ask Claude to build an Artifact with a clear chart, title that states the finding and labeled axes.

title: Research a company's context before a business case
how: Name the company and the case topic; ask Claude Research to collect recent public facts, competitors and risks, citing sources you can check.

title: Prepare for a workplace language proficiency test
how: Tell Claude the language and level; ask for speaking and writing prompts with feedback on grammar, register and business vocabulary.

title: Practice a translation or interpreting skills test
how: Ask for short business texts in both languages; translate them and have Claude flag inaccuracies, tone shifts and missing nuance.

title: Prepare for speed and accuracy tests for admin roles
how: Ask Claude for practice passages, shortcuts and a daily regimen that tracks speed and accuracy over a week.

title: Study for a compliance or safety knowledge test
how: Paste the regulations or handbook; ask Claude for flash questions, scenarios and a final mock test with explanations.

title: Build a bank of 8 STAR stories from your real history
how: Dump raw career notes and ask Claude to extract 8 situations, each in situation-task-action-result form with numbers; tag each by competency such as conflict, failure or leadership.

title: Map your stories to the questions a role will ask
how: Give your story bank and the posting; ask for a matrix of likely questions against the best story and a flagged list of questions with no good story yet.

title: Write a 90-second answer to tell me about yourself
how: Give resume, target role and one hook; ask for a past-present-future script of about 220 words, then a 45-second version, in spoken language.

title: Craft a specific answer to why do you want to work here
how: Paste your research notes and the posting; ask for a 60-second answer with two company-specific facts, one personal link and no flattery.

title: Prepare a calm answer to why are you leaving your job
how: Tell Claude the real reason; ask for a truthful forward-looking answer that does not criticize your employer, at 30 and 60 seconds.

title: Prepare an answer about being laid off
how: Share the circumstances and dates; ask for a concise, factual answer that moves to what you want next, with a follow-up for probing questions.

title: Build a real weakness answer with a concrete fix
how: List a true weakness and what you did about it; ask Claude to produce a 45-second answer showing self-awareness and progress, without a disguised strength.

title: Polish a failure story that shows learning
how: Tell Claude the failure, your role and what changed; ask for a 2-minute version with ownership, the lesson and a later example where you applied it.

title: Run a full mock interview in chat with scoring
how: Paste the posting and your resume; ask Claude to play the interviewer for 10 questions, one at a time, then give a score and one fix for each answer.

title: Practice answers aloud and review the transcript
how: Use voice mode or dictation to answer 8 questions, paste the transcript, and ask for feedback on structure, pace, filler words and answer length.

title: Rehearse with a skeptical or interrupting interviewer
how: Ask Claude to play a terse interviewer who challenges claims and asks why; practice staying calm and supplying evidence.

title: Prepare 8 smart questions for the interviewer
how: Give the role and the interviewer's title; ask for questions on success metrics, team, roadmap and risks, grouped by who should answer.

title: Brief yourself on your interviewers from public information
how: Paste public profile text of your interviewers; ask for a one-paragraph summary each, shared interests and a question tailored to their work.

title: Compile a one-page company brief before each interview
how: Name the company; ask Research for products, customers, recent news, competitors, funding and risks, with links, then a half-page of talking points.

title: Test the company's product and note observations
how: Describe what you tried in the product; ask Claude to turn it into three improvement ideas and a question for the product team.

title: Decode a job description into what the team actually needs
how: Paste the posting; ask Claude to rank duties, infer the pain behind the role, and list the five competencies the interview will probe.

title: Identify competency gaps and craft bridging answers
how: Share your background and the posting; ask Claude which asks are weak in your history and how to answer honestly using adjacent evidence.

title: Create the story of why you are changing fields
how: Give your old and new field and the motive; ask for a 60-second narrative that links past skills to the new role without apologizing.

title: Rehearse the salary expectations question in an interview
how: Give market data and your range; ask Claude to play the recruiter and practice three phrasings, including declining to give a number first.

title: Quantify accomplishments in your interview stories
how: Paste each story; ask Claude to ask you questions that reveal numbers (time, money, customers, error rate) and suggest honest estimates labeled as such.

title: Trim rambling answers to two minutes
how: Paste a transcript of a long answer; ask for a version at 120 seconds with the result first and the detail removed, then a 30-second backup.

title: Turn your stories and facts into flashcards
how: Give Claude your stories and company facts; ask for an Artifact of flashcards with prompts on one side and key points on the other.

title: Make a one-page cheat sheet for the interview
how: Give your notes; ask for a single page with your opening, top three proofs, questions to ask, interviewer names and logistics.

title: Plan interview preparation hour by hour
how: Give the interview date and hours available; ask for a schedule across research, stories, mock runs and rest, ending a day before.

title: Keep all interview prep in one Claude Project
how: Create a Project with your resume, story bank and each posting; ask Claude to answer questions only from those files and ask what is missing.

title: Prepare answers about company values and culture fit
how: Paste the company's stated values; ask for one genuine example per value from your past, and flag any you cannot back up.

title: Articulate your management philosophy with examples
how: Describe how you manage; ask for a 90-second answer with two examples, one on coaching and one on a hard personnel decision.

title: Draft a 30-60-90 day plan for an interview
how: Give the role, team and what you know; ask for a one-page plan that starts with listening and learning, then early wins, labeled as assumptions.

title: Prepare a story about disagreeing with a colleague
how: Share a real disagreement; ask Claude to shape it so you show empathy, evidence and the result, and to avoid blaming.

title: Prepare answers when you lack direct experience
how: List relevant coursework, projects and volunteering; ask for how to answer experience questions by bridging skills and showing quick learning.

title: Prepare for a first internship interview
how: Give your classes and projects; ask Claude to run 10 common questions for students, with advice on enthusiasm, learning goals and questions to ask.

title: Prepare a story set for executive-level interviews
how: Give Claude your biggest outcomes; ask for stories on strategy, turnaround, hiring, influencing up and a board-level result, each with scope and metrics.

title: Reframe experience to counter age assumptions
how: Paste your resume and share concerns; ask Claude to highlight recent learning, adaptability and current tools, and to prepare answers to overqualified concerns.

title: Prepare to answer the overqualified objection
how: Give your background and the target role; ask for a response that shows genuine motivation and a realistic path, plus follow-up questions.

title: Prepare to discuss a career break in interviews
how: Share the break and what you did; ask for a confident 40-second statement, a refresh plan and answers to what skills are rusty.

title: Build business Spanish vocabulary for your field
how: Name your field and the country; ask for 60 terms with usage sentences and common false friends, and quiz you on them.

title: Learn hiring etiquette for a specific Latin America country
how: Name the country and sector; ask Claude for norms on formality, titles, punctuality, small talk and dress, marked for verification with locals.

title: Prepare for remote-first company interview norms
how: Ask Claude for what remote employers look for: async writing, documentation habits, time-zone overlap, and rehearse answers about each.

title: Prepare a matrix of who will ask what on a panel
how: Give panelists' roles; ask Claude to predict each person's concerns and prepare an answer and a question per person.

title: Do a deep research pass on a company before a final round
how: Ask Research to cover the company's strategy, leadership interviews, financial health and layoffs, then a risk and opportunity summary with sources.

title: Summarize themes from public interview reviews
how: Paste excerpts of public interview reviews; ask Claude to group them into question types and process steps, noting reviews can be unreliable.

title: Set prep reminders before every interview
how: With the Calendar connector, ask Claude to add research, mock and rest blocks ahead of each interview and a 15-minute pre-brief.

title: Pull a brief from recruiter email threads before the call
how: With the Gmail connector, ask Claude to summarize the thread with a recruiter: role details, names, stages, salary hints and open questions.

title: Create a scoring rubric to self-assess mock answers
how: Ask Claude to build a 5-point rubric for structure, evidence, relevance, concision and tone, then rate your recorded answers.

title: Keep an interview journal to improve between rounds
how: After each interview paste your notes; ask Claude to log questions asked, your weak answers and the next fix, and to show patterns over time.

title: Prepare a pre-interview calming routine
how: Describe how nerves show up; ask for a 5-minute routine with breathing, a reframing sentence and a first-answer opener you know cold.

title: Prepare for the recruiter phone screen
how: Paste the posting and your resume; ask Claude to run a 15-minute screen covering motivation, salary, timeline and logistics, then script concise answers.

title: Prepare for a first call with the hiring manager
how: Give the posting and any manager info; ask for the three problems they likely want solved, matching stories and questions that reveal their priorities.

title: Drill a behavioral round with follow-up probes
how: Ask Claude to ask 8 behavioral questions and after each answer probe with what exactly did you do and what happened; score the specificity.

title: Practice talking through a technical screen out loud
how: Choose a problem type; ask Claude to act as the interviewer, withhold hints at first, then give feedback on how clearly you reasoned.

title: Practice a live consulting-style case interview
how: Ask Claude to deliver a case verbally in pieces with data on request; practice structure, math, synthesis and a final recommendation.

title: Sharpen mental math for case interviews
how: Ask for 20 quick calculations on growth, margins and break-even; time yourself and have Claude explain shortcuts for each.

title: Plan how to handle a panel interview
how: Give the panel composition; ask for eye contact rules, how to split answers, who to address and a closing question for each member.

title: Rehearse a presentation interview with Q and A
how: Paste your slides' text; ask Claude to time each section, play an unconvinced panel and ask five hard questions with feedback on your answers.

title: Script a portfolio walkthrough for design or creative roles
how: Give your three best projects; ask for a 3-minute narrative each covering problem, your role, decisions, results and what you would change.

title: Drill a system design interview with an AI interviewer
how: Ask Claude to pose a design prompt, answer your clarifying questions and push on scaling, failure modes and cost; then review your structure.

title: Practice pair programming with Claude as the partner
how: Run a Claude Code session on a small task while explaining your thinking; ask afterward for feedback on collaboration, testing habits and naming.

title: Practice a debugging interview with planted bugs
how: Ask Claude Code to create a small repo with three bugs; find and explain them aloud and then review your method.

title: Prepare behavioral stories specific to engineering roles
how: Give your project history; ask for stories on production incidents, technical disagreements, mentoring and prioritization with results.

title: Practice the sell me this product exercise
how: Ask Claude to choose a random object and play the customer; sell with discovery questions first and get feedback on value framing.

title: Prepare your quota attainment story and pipeline math
how: Give your numbers; ask Claude to tell the story of attainment, deal sizes, cycle length and a lost deal lesson, with figures reconciled.

title: Practice customer success scenarios and renewals questions
how: Ask Claude to simulate an at-risk account conversation and a renewal discussion; get feedback on diagnosis, empathy and next steps.

title: Practice product manager interview question types
how: Choose a type such as execution, strategy or metrics; ask Claude for a question, a framework-free critique and a better answer outline.

title: Practice metrics and root-cause questions
how: Ask for prompts like why did signups drop 10 percent; walk through hypotheses and data checks, then compare with Claude's structure.

title: Prepare for people-management interview questions
how: Ask Claude to role-play a director asking about firing, underperformance, hiring and team morale; rehearse with specific examples.

title: Prepare for executive and board conversations
how: Give the company's situation; ask Claude to play a board member probing strategy, risk and leadership style with direct questions.

title: Run a full interview in Spanish with a native-style interviewer
how: Tell Claude the country and role; ask for a 20-minute Spanish interview, then corrections on grammar, register and vocabulary.

title: Practice switching languages mid-interview
how: Ask Claude to alternate questions between Spanish and English; practice answering in the language asked and showing business fluency.

title: Prepare a short demonstration of professional fluency
how: Ask for a 3-minute talk topic in your field in your second language; rehearse, record and get feedback on clarity and tone.

title: Check setup and delivery for a video interview
how: Describe your room and tools; ask for a checklist for camera height, lighting, audio, background, backup plan and screen sharing.

title: Plan an on-site interview day
how: Paste the itinerary; ask for a timeline, travel buffer, questions for each session and energy plan including lunch and breaks.

title: Prepare for a group interview with other candidates
how: Describe the format; ask Claude to simulate it and suggest ways to contribute, build on others and stand out without dominating.

title: Prepare for a meal interview
how: Ask Claude for ordering choices, conversation pacing and what to avoid; rehearse small talk questions.

title: Prepare for an informal chat that is actually an interview
how: Give the contact's role; ask Claude to prepare a concise pitch, three curious questions and a way to ask about openings gracefully.

title: Prepare a 30-second pitch and questions for a career fair
how: Give your background and the exhibitor list; ask for a pitch, a question per booth and a way to ask for a next step.

title: Prepare for on-campus recruiting interviews
how: Give your major and target firms; ask for common questions, rehearse answers using coursework and extracurricular stories.

title: Prepare for an internal promotion or transfer interview

how: Give the courses you want; ask for a request with the business case and amount, as a low-cost add the employer can grant.

how: Describe why you wanted to leave and what they offered; ask for a decision frame on reasons that remain, risks and a pro-con analysis.

how: Give the final terms; ask for a short acceptance that confirms details, start date and onboarding steps.
